1	# External Agents for Entire CLI
2	
3	This repository contains standalone external agent binaries that extend the [Entire CLI](https://github.com/entireio/cli) with support for additional AI coding agents.
4	
5	## What Are External Agents?
6	
7	External agents are standalone binaries (named `entire-agent-<name>`) that teach Entire CLI how to work with AI coding agents it doesn't natively support. When an external agent is installed on your `PATH`, Entire discovers it automatically and gains the ability to:
8	
9	- **Create checkpoints** during AI coding sessions so you can rewind mistakes
10	- **Capture transcripts** of what the AI agent did and why
11	- **Install hooks** so the AI agent's lifecycle events (start, stop, commit) flow through Entire
12	
13	External agents communicate with Entire CLI via subcommands that accept and return JSON over stdin/stdout. See the [external agent protocol spec](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/docs/architecture/external-agent-protocol.md) for the full interface.
14	
15	## Available Agents
16	
17	| Agent | Directory | Status |
18	|-------|-----------|--------|
19	| [Kiro](agents/entire-agent-kiro/) | `agents/entire-agent-kiro/` | Implemented — hooks + transcript analysis |
20	| [Pi](agents/entire-agent-pi/) | `agents/entire-agent-pi/` | Implemented — hooks + transcript analysis + token calculation + compact transcripts |
21	
22	See each agent's own README for setup and usage instructions.
23	
24	## Building a New External Agent
25	
26	This repo includes a skill that guides you through building a new external agent with two test layers:
27	
28	1. **Protocol compliance** — generic subcommand coverage from [`entireio/external-agents-tests`](https://github.com/entireio/external-agents-tests)
29	2. **Lifecycle integration** — repo-local `e2e/` tests that exercise `entire enable`, prompt execution, checkpoints, and rewind
30	3. **Implementation** — build the binary until both layers pass, then add unit tests
31	
32	### Getting Started — Zero Setup
33	
34	Clone the repo and open it in your AI coding tool. Each tool auto-discovers the skill with no additional configuration:
35	
36	| Tool | How it discovers | What to say |
37	|------|-----------------|-------------|
38	| **Claude Code** | `.claude/skills/` directory | `/entire-external-agent` |
39	| **Codex** | `AGENTS.md` at project root | "Build an external agent" |
40	| **Cursor** | `.cursor/rules/` directory | "Build an external agent" |
41	| **OpenCode** | `.opencode/plugins/` auto-loaded | "Build an external agent" |
42	
43	The skill files live in `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/` if you want to read the details.
44	
45	## Testing
46	
47	Testing is intentionally split:
48	
49	- **Generic protocol checks** run in GitHub Actions via [`entireio/external-agents-tests`](https://github.com/entireio/external-agents-tests). The workflow builds each `entire-agent-*` binary in this repo and runs the shared compliance suite against it.
50	- **Agent unit/build checks** run in GitHub Actions for every `agents/entire-agent-*` directory discovered at runtime.
51	- **Lifecycle tests** stay in this repo's [`e2e/`](e2e/) harness. These verify the parts that depend on Entire itself and on the real agent CLI: prompt execution, hook installation after `entire enable`, checkpoint creation, rewind behavior, and interactive sessions.
52	- **Unit tests** live with each agent implementation under [`agents/`](agents/).
53	
54	### Running Tests
55	
56	```bash
57	# Run default test suite for all agents
58	mise run test
59	
60	# Same as test, kept for explicit CI-style naming
61	mise run test:ci
62	
63	# Run lifecycle integration tests from this repo
64	mise run test:e2e
65	
66	# Same as test:e2e, kept as the explicit name
67	mise run test:e2e:lifecycle
68	```
69	
70	Protocol compliance runs in CI through [`.github/workflows/protocol-compliance.yml`](.github/workflows/protocol-compliance.yml).
71	
72	For a newly added agent to be picked up automatically by local root tasks and CI, add `agents/entire-agent-<name>/mise.toml` with `build` and `test` tasks. The shared runner falls back to Go defaults when `go.mod` exists, but the `mise` tasks are the contract for non-standard setups.
73	
74	### Lifecycle Harness Architecture
75	
76	The lifecycle harness auto-discovers and builds all agents in `agents/` via `TestMain`:
77	
78	| File | Purpose |
79	|------|---------|
80	| `e2e/setup_test.go` | `TestMain` entry point — discovers agents, builds binaries, configures PATH |
81	| `e2e/lifecycle_test.go` | Shared lifecycle scenarios run against every registered agent |
82	| `e2e/agents/` | Agent adapters for the real CLIs used during lifecycle tests |
83	| `e2e/entire/` | Entire CLI wrappers used by lifecycle assertions |
84	| `e2e/testutil/` | Repo setup, artifact capture, git helpers, and checkpoint assertions |
85	
86	### Environment Variables
87	
88	| Variable | Description |
89	|----------|-------------|
90	| `E2E_ENTIRE_BIN` | Path to the `entire` binary (defaults to `entire` from PATH) |
91	| `E2E_AGENT` | Filter lifecycle runs to a single registered agent |
92	| `E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR` | Override lifecycle artifact output directory |
93	| `E2E_KEEP_REPOS` | Preserve temp repos for debugging |
94	| `E2E_CONCURRENT_TEST_LIMIT` | Override the per-agent lifecycle concurrency limit |
95	
96	## Repository Layout
97	
98	```
99	agents/                          # Standalone external agent projects
100	  entire-agent-kiro/             # Kiro agent (Go binary)
101	  entire-agent-pi/               # Pi agent (Go binary)
102	e2e/                             # Lifecycle integration harness
103	.github/workflows/               # CI, including protocol compliance via external-agents-tests
104	.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/  # Skill files (research, test-writer, implementer)
105	AGENTS.md                        # Codex auto-discovery
106	.cursor/rules/                   # Cursor auto-discovery
107	.opencode/plugins/               # OpenCode auto-discovery
108	```

1	# External Agent Builder
2	
3	This repository includes a skill that guides you through building standalone external agent binaries for the [Entire CLI](https://github.com/entireio/cli). The current testing split is:
4	
5	- Protocol compliance in `external-agents-tests`
6	- Lifecycle integration in this repo's `e2e/` harness
7	- Agent-specific unit tests in each `agents/entire-agent-*` module
8	
9	## Available Commands
10	
11	| Command | Skill file | Description |
12	|---------|-----------|-------------|
13	| Full pipeline | `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/SKILL.md` | Run all three phases sequentially |
14	| Research | `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/research.md` | Analyze the target agent's capabilities and map to the protocol |
15	| Write tests | `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/write-tests.md` | Scaffold the binary and wire protocol compliance plus lifecycle coverage |
16	| Implement | `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/implement.md` | Build the binary using protocol compliance first, lifecycle second, unit tests last |
17	
18	## How to Use
19	
20	When the user asks to "build an external agent", "create an agent binary", or "external agent plugin":
21	
22	1. Read `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/SKILL.md` for the full pipeline overview
23	2. Follow the three phases in order: research, write-tests, implement
24	3. Each phase has a dedicated skill file with detailed instructions
25	4. Keep reusable protocol checks out of this repo's `e2e/` directory. Add them to `external-agents-tests` instead.
26	
27	## Tool Mapping (Codex)
28	
29	The skill files reference Claude Code tool names. Map them to Codex equivalents:
30	
31	| Skill references | Codex equivalent |
32	|-----------------|-----------------|
33	| `TodoWrite` | `update_plan` |
34	| `Task` / subagent launches | Codex's native subagent system |
35	| `Skill` tool | Read the skill file directly |
36	| `Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `Bash` | Native Codex tools |
37	
38	## Protocol Spec
39	
40	The external agent protocol is defined at:
41	`https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/docs/architecture/external-agent-protocol.md`

1	# Contributing to the Entire CLI
2	
3	Thank you for your interest in contributing to Entire! We welcome contributions from everyone.
4	
5	Please read our [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) before participating.
6	
7	> **New to Entire?** See the [First-Time Contributors guide](docs/first-time-contributors.md) for a step-by-step first contribution walkthrough, or the [README](README.md) for setup and usage documentation.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Before You Code: Discuss First
12	
13	The fastest way to get a contribution merged is to align with maintainers before writing code. Please **open an issue first** using our [issue templates](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/new/choose) and wait for maintainer feedback before starting implementation.
14	
15	### Contribution Workflow
16	
17	1. **Open an issue** describing the problem or feature
18	2. **Wait for maintainer feedback** -- we may have relevant context or plans
19	3. **Get approval** before starting implementation
20	4. **Submit your PR** referencing the approved issue
21	5. **Address all feedback** including automated Copilot comments
22	6. **Maintainer review and merge**
23	
24	---
25	
26	## First-Time Contributors
27	
28	New to the project? Welcome! Start with the
29	[First-Time Contributors guide](docs/first-time-contributors.md). It explains
30	how to find a comfortable issue, ask for a scoped starter task, set up the repo,
31	use AI responsibly, run the right checks, and open your first pull request.
32	
33	### Starter Contributions
34	
35	We recommend starting with:
36	
37	- **A bug you can reproduce** - Add the missing test and a narrow fix
38	- **CLI output improvements** - Clarify confusing messages or help text
39	- **Test contributions** - Cover existing behavior with a focused test
40	- **Setup friction** - Improve README or contributor instructions after you hit a real problem
41	
42	Browse [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues), or ask in the
43	`#looking-for-contributors` Discord channel if you want help finding a
44	starter-sized slice.
45	
46	Using a coding agent while contributing is welcome, but you are responsible for
47	the final diff. Review AI-generated changes yourself before opening a PR.
48	
49	---
50	
51	## Submitting Issues
52	
53	All feature requests, bug reports, and general issues should be submitted through [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues). Please search for existing issues before opening a new one.
54	
55	For security-related issues, see the Security section below.
56	
57	---
58	
59	## Security
60	
61	If you discover a security vulnerability, **do not report it through GitHub Issues**. Instead, please follow the instructions in our [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) file for responsible disclosure. All security reports are kept confidential as described in SECURITY.md.
62	
63	---
64	
65	## Contributions & Communication
66	
67	Contributions and communications are expected to occur through:
68	
69	- [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) - Bug reports and feature requests
70	- [Discord](https://discord.gg/jZJs3Tue4S) - Questions, general conversation, and real-time support
71	
72	Please represent the project and community respectfully in all public and private interactions.
73	
74	
75	## How to Contribute
76	
77	
78	There are many ways to contribute:
79	
80	- **Feature requests** - Open a [GitHub Issue](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) to discuss your idea
81	- **Bug reports** - Report issues via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) (see [Reporting Bugs](#reporting-bugs))
82	- **Code contributions** - Fix bugs, add features, improve tests
83	- **Documentation** - Improve guides, fix typos, add examples
84	- **Community** - Help others, answer questions, share knowledge
85	
86	
87	## Reporting Bugs
88	
89	Good bug reports help us fix issues quickly. When reporting a bug, please include:
90	
91	### Required Information
92	
93	1. **Entire CLI version** - run `entire version`
94	2. **Operating system**
95	3. **Go version** - run `go version`
96	
97	### What to Include
98	
99	Please answer these questions in your bug report:
100	
101	1. **What did you do?** - Include the exact commands you ran
102	2. **What did you expect to happen?**
103	3. **What actually happened?** - Include the full error message or unexpected output
104	4. **Can you reproduce it?** - Does it happen every time or intermittently?
105	5. **Any additional context?** - Logs, screenshots, or related issues
106	
107	---
108	
109	## Local Setup
110	
111	### Prerequisites
112	
113	- **Go 1.26.x** - Check with `go version`
114	- **mise** - Task runner and version manager. Install with `curl https://mise.run | sh`
115	
116	### Clone and Install
117	
118	```bash
119	# Clone the repository
120	git clone https://github.com/entireio/cli.git
121	cd cli
122	
123	# Trust the mise configuration (required on first setup)
124	mise trust
125	
126	# Install dependencies (mise will install the correct Go version)
127	mise install
128	
129	# Download Go modules
130	go mod download
131	
132	# Build the CLI
133	mise run build
134	
135	# Verify setup by running tests
136	mise run test
137	```
138	
139	> See [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) for detailed architecture and development reference.
140	
141	---
142	
143	## Making Changes
144	
145	1. **Create a branch** for your changes:
146	   ```bash
147	   git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name
148	   ```
149	
150	2. **Make your changes** - follow the [Code Style](#code-style) guidelines
151	
152	3. **Test your changes** - see [Testing](#testing)
153	
154	4. **Commit** with clear, descriptive messages:
155	   ```bash
156	   git commit -m "Add feature: description of what you added"
157	   ```
158	
159	---
160	
161	## Code Style
162	
163	Follow standard Go idioms and conventions. For detailed guidance, see the **Go Code Style** section in [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md).
164	
165	### Key Points
166	
167	- **Error handling**: Handle all errors explicitly - don't leave them unchecked
168	- **Formatting**: Code must pass `gofmt` (run `mise run fmt`)
169	- **Linting**: Code must pass `golangci-lint` (run `mise run lint`)
170	- **Naming**: Use meaningful, descriptive names following Go conventions
171	
172	---
173	
174	## Testing
175	
176	> See [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) for complete testing documentation.
177	
178	```bash
179	# Unit tests - always run before committing
180	mise run test
181	
182	# Integration tests
183	mise run test:integration
184	
185	# Full CI suite
186	mise run test:ci
187	```
188	
189	Integration tests use the `//go:build integration` build tag and are located in `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/`.
190	
191	---
192	
193	## Creating an Agent
194	
195	
196	Entire supports two ways to create agents:
197	
198	### 1. Claude Code Agent Personas (Markdown)
199	
200	These are markdown files that define specialized behaviors for Claude Code (e.g., developer, reviewer, etc.).
201	
202	- **Location:** `.claude/agents/`
203	- **Structure:**
204	   ```markdown
205	   ---
206	   name: my-agent
207	   description: What this agent does
208	   model: opus
209	   color: blue
210	   ---
211	
212	   # Agent Name
213	   You are a **[Role]** with expertise in [domain].
214	
215	   ## Core Principles
216	   - Principle 1
217	   - Principle 2
218	
219	   ## Process
220	   1. Step 1
221	   2. Step 2
222	
223	   ## Output Format
224	   How to structure responses...
225	   ```
226	- **To invoke:** Create a matching command in `.claude/commands/` that spawns the agent via the Task tool.
227	- **Examples:**
228	   - `.claude/agents/dev.md` - TDD Developer
229	   - `.claude/agents/reviewer.md` - Code Reviewer
230	
231	### 2. Coding Agent Integrations (Go)
232	
233	These are Go implementations that integrate Entire with different AI coding tools (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI, etc.) using the Agent abstraction layer.
234	
235	- **Location:** `cmd/entire/cli/agent/`
236	- **Steps:**
237	   1. Implement the `Agent` interface in `agent/agent.go`
238	   2. Register your agent in the agent registry
239	   3. Add setup and hook configuration as needed
240	   4. Ensure session and checkpoint tracking is handled per the abstraction
241	- **Reference:** See [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) for architecture and code examples.
242	
243	---
244	
245	**Which should I use?**
246	
247	- Use a persona markdown agent if you want to create a new role or workflow for Claude Code.
248	- Use a coding agent integration if you want to add support for a new AI coding tool or extend agent capabilities in the CLI.
249	
250	---
251	
252	## Submitting a Pull Request
253	
254	### Before You Submit
255	
256	- **Related issue exists and is approved** -- Your PR references an issue where a maintainer has acknowledged the approach. (Exceptions: typo corrections, wording-only updates, and maintainer-scoped starter tasks.)
257	- **Linting passes** -- Run `mise run lint` (includes golangci-lint, gofmt, gomod, shellcheck)
258	- **Tests pass** -- Run `mise run test` to verify your changes
259	- **Tests included** -- New Go code and functionality should have accompanying tests
260	- **Entire checkpoint trailers included** -- See [Using Entire While Contributing](#using-entire-while-contributing) below
261	
262	PRs that skip these steps are likely to be closed without merge.
263	
264	### Submitting
265	
266	1. **Push** your branch to your fork
267	2. **Open a PR** against the `main` branch
268	3. **Describe your changes** -- Link the related issue, summarize what changed and what testing you did
269	4. **Address Copilot feedback** -- See [Responding to Automated Review](#responding-to-automated-review)
270	5. **Wait for maintainer review**
271	
272	---
273	
274	## Responding to Automated Review
275	
276	Co-pilot agent reviews every PR and provides feedback on code quality, potential bugs, and project conventions.
277	
278	**Read and respond to every Copilot comment.** PRs with unaddressed Copilot feedback will not move to maintainer review.
279	
280	- **Fixed** -- Push a commit addressing the issue.
281	- **Disagree** -- Reply explaining your reasoning. The Copilot isn't always right.
282	- **Question** -- Ask for clarification. We're happy to help.
283	
284	Addressing Copilot feedback upfront is the fastest path to maintainer review.
285	
286	---
287	
288	## Using Entire While Contributing
289	
290	We use Entire on Entire. When contributing, install the Entire CLI and let it capture your coding sessions -- this gives us valuable dogfooding data and helps improve the tool.
291	
292	### Setup
293	
294	Install the latest version of the Entire CLI (see [installation docs](https://docs.entire.io/cli/installation)) and verify with `entire version`. Entire is already configured in this repository, so there's no need to run `entire enable`.
295	
296	### Checkpoint Trailers
297	
298	All commits should include `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers from your sessions. These are added automatically by the `prepare-commit-msg` hook when Entire is enabled. The trailers link your commits to session metadata on the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch.
299	
300	### Sessions Branch
301	
302	When you push your PR branch, Entire can automatically push the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch alongside it (if `push_sessions` is enabled in your settings). Include this in your PR so maintainers can review the session context behind your changes.
303

1	# First-Time Contributors
2	
3	Welcome. This guide is for people who are new to Entire, new to open source, or
4	just want a careful path through their first contribution to this repository.
5	
6	The main contribution rules live in [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md). Treat
7	that file as the source of truth. This page slows the process down and explains
8	where to start, what to say, what to run, and what to expect after you open a
9	pull request.
10	
11	## Who This Is For
12	
13	Start here if any of these are true:
14	
15	- You have never opened a pull request before.
16	- You have contributed to other projects, but not to Entire.
17	- You want help finding a contribution that is small enough to finish.
18	- You are unsure how to ask maintainers for the right amount of context.
19	
20	If you are already comfortable with this repo, use the shorter workflow in
21	[CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md).
22	
23	## Choose a First Contribution
24	
25	Start by browsing [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) for
26	issues that describe behavior you can reproduce, mention a command or workflow
27	you can try locally, or feel concrete enough that you can explain the problem
28	back in your own words. You can also check the `#looking-for-contributors`
29	channel in Discord. You do not need to understand the whole project before
30	asking about an issue.
31	
32	Good first contributions are small, clear, and easy to review. For this repo,
33	that usually means one of these:
34	
35	- Reproducing a bug you personally hit and adding the missing test.
36	- Clarifying a confusing CLI message, help text, or setup step.
37	- Adding a focused test around existing command behavior.
38	- Fixing a small platform-specific issue on macOS, Linux, or Windows.
39	- Improving README or contributor instructions after you hit real friction.
40	
41	When looking at an issue, favor ones where you can explain the problem back in
42	your own words. It is okay if you do not know the fix yet. If an issue is broad,
43	comment with the part you think you can tackle and ask whether that slice would
44	be useful.
45	
46	If you do not already have a specific problem in mind, ask in
47	`#looking-for-contributors` and mention what you are comfortable with, such as
48	Go tests, CLI output, setup issues, Windows behavior, or README/contributor
49	wording. A maintainer can usually point you toward a safer slice than browsing
50	alone can.
51	
52	As a first PR, avoid broad architecture changes, new agent integrations, command
53	renames, checkpoint strategy changes, or anything that changes git history
54	behavior unless a maintainer has already helped define the scope.
55	
56	## Comment Before You Start
57	
58	Before starting non-trivial code work, leave a short comment on the issue or
59	start a new issue. This helps avoid duplicated effort and gives maintainers a
60	chance to redirect you before you spend time on the wrong approach.
61	
62	A good first comment is specific:
63	
64	```text
65	Hi, I am new to Entire and would like to work on this.
66	
67	I was able to reproduce the issue by running:
68	
69	  entire status
70	
71	My plan is to update the error message in <file or command area> and add a
72	focused test for the behavior. Does that sound like the right direction?
73	```
74	
75	If you are not starting from an existing issue, open one with the smallest
76	concrete problem you can describe:
77	
78	```text
79	I hit confusing behavior while running `entire enable` on macOS.
80	
81	Expected: the command would explain which agent config was missing.
82	Actual: the command exited with "not configured".
83	
84	I can reproduce this locally. Would a small PR that improves the message and
85	adds a focused test be useful?
86	```
87	
88	You do not need a perfect plan. Showing what you have tried and where you are
89	headed is usually enough.
90	
91	## Set Up the Repository
92	
93	Fork the repository on GitHub, then clone your fork:
94	
95	```bash
96	git clone git@github.com:YOUR-USERNAME/cli.git
97	cd cli
98	```
99	
100	Add the upstream repository so you can pull in maintainer changes later:
101	
102	```bash
103	git remote add upstream git@github.com:entireio/cli.git
104	git fetch upstream
105	```
106	
107	Install the local toolchain:
108	
109	```bash
110	mise trust
111	mise install
112	go mod download
113	mise run build
114	```
115	
116	Verify the setup with the normal test suite:
117	
118	```bash
119	mise run test
120	```
121	
122	If setup fails, include the command you ran, the full error text, your OS, and
123	the output of `go version` when asking for help.
124	
125	## Create a Branch
126	
127	Create a branch from the latest `main`:
128	
129	```bash
130	git switch main
131	git pull upstream main
132	git switch -c fix/clearer-enable-error
133	```
134	
135	Use a branch name that describes the change. Examples:
136	
137	- `fix/clearer-enable-error`
138	- `test/session-status-output`
139	- `docs/setup-troubleshooting-note`
140	
141	## Make a Small Change
142	
143	Keep your first pull request narrow. A focused PR is easier to review and easier
144	to finish.
145	
146	Good first PR shapes:
147	
148	- One failing behavior plus its test.
149	- One small error message improvement.
150	- One test-only clarification.
151	- One README or setup clarification based on a real problem you hit.
152	
153	Avoid bundling unrelated cleanup with your first PR. If you notice extra things
154	while working, leave yourself a note and open a follow-up issue or PR later.
155	
156	## Use AI Carefully
157	
158	Entire CLI is not an agent. It is a CLI for capturing and navigating AI-agent
159	work, so it is completely normal to use coding agents while contributing.
160	There is no need to tell us that you used AI in your work.
161	
162	Use whatever agent and workflow you like. We hope you like Goose, of course. The
163	important rule is that you are responsible for the final code, tests, and docs.
164	Before submitting a PR, review the diff yourself. PRs that look generated,
165	unreviewed, or "vibe coded" without a human pass may be closed.
166	
167	Quick responsible AI tips:
168	
169	- **Think first.** Agents tend to jump straight to code. Ask the agent to explore
170	  the codebase first, explain the relevant architecture, and propose an approach
171	  before it edits files.
172	- **Push back on shortcuts.** Watch for trivial tests, overly wide types,
173	  optional fields added just to satisfy the compiler, swallowed errors, and
174	  copied local patterns that do not actually fit.
175	- **Notice uncertainty.** If the agent keeps declaring that it understands the
176	  issue but the patches are not converging, stop and reframe the task. Use what
177	  you learned to start a smaller attempt.
178	- **Cut the bloat.** Remove redundant comments, just-in-case logging,
179	  over-defensive branches, and tests that only check implementation details
180	  instead of user-visible behavior.
181	
182	## Run the Right Checks
183	
184	For wording-only changes, run a lightweight sanity check:
185	
186	```bash
187	git diff --check
188	```
189	
190	For Go code changes, run:
191	
192	```bash
193	mise run fmt
194	mise run lint
195	mise run test
196	```
197	
198	Before a larger PR or when a maintainer asks for full verification, run:
199	
200	```bash
201	mise run check
202	```
203	
204	Do not run real agent E2E tests unless a maintainer explicitly asks you to. They
205	can make real agent API calls. The deterministic canary E2E suite is safe to run
206	when your change touches E2E prompt wording or test infrastructure:
207	
208	```bash
209	mise run test:e2e:canary
210	```
211	
212	## Commit Your Work
213	
214	Commit with a short, descriptive message:
215	
216	```bash
217	git add <files you changed>
218	git commit -m "Clarify enable error when agent config is missing"
219	```
220	
221	Entire is used to dogfood Entire. If you have the Entire CLI installed and
222	enabled in this repository, the git hook may add an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer
223	to your commit message automatically. That is expected. See
224	[Using Entire While Contributing](../CONTRIBUTING.md#using-entire-while-contributing)
225	for the full details.
226	
227	## Open a Pull Request
228	
229	Push your branch to your fork:
230	
231	```bash
232	git push -u origin fix/clearer-enable-error
233	```
234	
235	Then open a pull request against `entireio/cli` on GitHub.
236	
237	In the PR description, include:
238	
239	- The issue it addresses, if there is one.
240	- A short summary of what changed.
241	- The checks you ran, such as `mise run test` or `git diff --check`.
242	- Anything you want reviewers to pay special attention to.
243	
244	If your PR is not ready for final review yet, open it as a draft. Draft PRs are
245	useful when you want early feedback on direction.
246	
247	## Respond to Review
248	
249	Review is part of the contribution, not a sign that you did something wrong.
250	Entire PRs may receive automated Copilot comments and maintainer comments.
251	
252	For each review comment:
253	
254	- If it is right, push a follow-up commit that addresses it.
255	- If you are unsure, ask a question on the PR.
256	- If you disagree, explain your reasoning briefly and respectfully.
257	
258	After pushing updates, leave a short comment saying what changed. GitHub does
259	not always make it obvious which comments were addressed by a new commit.
260	
261	## If You Get Stuck
262	
263	Ask early, and include context. Good help requests include:
264	
265	- What you are trying to do.
266	- The command you ran.
267	- The exact error or output.
268	- What you already checked.
269	- Your OS and Go version when setup or tests are involved.
270	
271	Useful places to ask:
272	
273	- The GitHub issue you are working on.
274	- The pull request, if one is already open.
275	- [Discord](https://discord.gg/jZJs3Tue4S) for general questions.
276	
277	## Quick Checklist
278	
279	Before opening your first PR:
280	
281	- You picked a small, focused change.
282	- You asked for maintainer scope before non-trivial code work.
283	- You created a branch from current `main`.
284	- You ran the checks that match your change.
285	- Your PR description explains what changed and how you tested it.
286	
287	Thank you for taking the time to contribute. Small, careful improvements make
288	the project easier for the next person too.

# Contributing to Entire External Agents

Thank you for your interest in contributing! This repository hosts the standalone
external agent binaries (`entire-agent-<name>`) that extend the
[Entire CLI](https://github.com/entireio/cli) with support for additional AI
coding agents.

Please read the [Entire CLI Code of Conduct](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
before participating.

> **New to Entire?** See the [First-Time Contributors guide](doc/first-time-contributors.md)
> for a step-by-step first contribution walkthrough, or the [README](README.md)
> for setup and architecture documentation.

---

## Before You Code: Discuss First

The fastest way to get a contribution merged is to align with maintainers before
writing code. Please **open an issue first** describing what you want to change,
and wait for maintainer feedback before starting implementation. This is
especially true for new external agents -- adding a new `entire-agent-<name>` is
a long-running commitment that the maintainers will need to support.

### Contribution Workflow

1. **Open an issue** describing the problem, feature, or new agent
2. **Wait for maintainer feedback** -- we may have relevant context or plans
3. **Get approval** before starting implementation
4. **Submit your PR** referencing the approved issue
5. **Address all feedback** including automated Copilot comments
6. **Maintainer review and merge**

---

## First-Time Contributors

New to the project? Welcome! Start with the
[First-Time Contributors guide](doc/first-time-contributors.md). It explains
how to find a comfortable issue, ask for a scoped starter task, set up the
repo, use AI responsibly, run the right checks, and open your first pull
request.

Issues**. Instead, follow the disclosure process described in the
[Entire CLI SECURITY.md](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
All security reports are kept confidential.

## Communication

Contributions and communications are expected to occur through:

- [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/external-agents/issues) -- Bug
  reports and feature requests
- [Discord](https://discord.gg/jZJs3Tue4S) -- Questions, general conversation,
  and real-time support

Please represent the project and community respectfully in all public and
private interactions.

## How to Contribute

There are many ways to contribute:

- **Fix or extend an existing agent** -- `entire-agent-kiro` or
  `entire-agent-pi` under [`agents/`](agents/)
- **Improve the lifecycle harness** -- The shared `e2e/` tests that exercise
  every agent
- **Add a new external agent** -- Discuss in an issue first; the
  [external agent builder skill](.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/) walks
  you through the full pipeline
- **Documentation** -- Improve READMEs, agent docs, contributor instructions
- **Community** -- Help others on Discord, answer questions, share knowledge

## Reporting Bugs

Good bug reports help us fix issues quickly. When reporting a bug, please
include:

### Required Information

1. **Affected agent** -- e.g. `entire-agent-kiro`, `entire-agent-pi`, or "the
   `e2e/` harness"
2. **Entire CLI version** -- run `entire version`
3. **Operating system**
4. **Go version** -- run `go version`
5. **mise version** -- run `mise --version`

### What to Include

1. **What did you do?** -- Include the exact commands you ran
2. **What did you expect to happen?**
3. **What actually happened?** -- Include the full error message or unexpected
   output (especially the JSON returned by the agent if a protocol check
   failed)
4. **Can you reproduce it?** -- Does it happen every time or intermittently?
5. **Any additional context?** -- Logs, lifecycle artifacts from
   `e2e/artifacts/`, related issues

## Local Setup

### Prerequisites

- **Go 1.26.x** -- mise will install the pinned version
- **mise** -- Task runner and version manager. Install with
  `curl https://mise.run | sh`
- **The target agent's own CLI** if you plan to run lifecycle tests against it

### Clone and Install

```bash
# Clone the repository

cd external-agents

# Trust the mise configuration (required on first setup)
mise trust

# Install pinned tools (Go, golangci-lint, license_finder, ...)
mise install

# Build every agent binary into ./bin
mise run build

# Verify setup by running unit tests across all agents
mise run test
```

Follow standard Go idioms and conventions.

### Key Points

- **Error handling**: Handle all errors explicitly -- don't leave them
  unchecked.
- **Formatting**: Code must pass `gofmt` (run `mise run fmt`).
- **Linting**: Code must pass `golangci-lint`. The config lives at
  [.golangci.yaml](.golangci.yaml).
- **Naming**: Use meaningful, descriptive names following Go conventions.
- **Protocol surface**: When changing a subcommand's JSON output, keep it
  compatible with the [external agent protocol spec](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/docs/architecture/external-agent-protocol.md).
  Add or update protocol-compliance coverage in
  [`entireio/external-agents-tests`](https://github.com/entireio/external-agents-tests)
  in the same PR cycle.

---

## Testing

Testing is intentionally split into three layers (see [README](README.md) for
the full picture):

| Layer | Where it lives | When to run |
|-------|----------------|-------------|
| Protocol compliance | `entireio/external-agents-tests` (run in CI via [protocol-compliance.yml](.github/workflows/protocol-compliance.yml)) | When you change subcommand JSON, exit codes, or protocol surface |
| Lifecycle integration | `e2e/` in this repo | When you change anything that interacts with `entire enable`, hooks, checkpoints, or rewind |
| Unit | `agents/entire-agent-*/` | Always, before pushing |

```bash
# Unit tests across all agents (default suite)
mise run test

# Lifecycle integration tests against every registered agent
mise run test:e2e

# Same as test:e2e, kept as the explicit name
mise run test:e2e:lifecycle

# Limit lifecycle runs to one agent while iterating
E2E_AGENT=kiro mise run test:e2e
```

CI also runs the protocol compliance suite against every built binary. You do
not normally need to run that locally, but you can mirror it with:

```bash
# After mise run build, run the shared compliance suite against one binary
external-agents-tests --binary-path ./bin/entire-agent-kiro
```

The lifecycle harness calls the real agent CLIs, so the corresponding tool
(`kiro`, `pi`, ...) must be on your PATH. See each agent's README for setup
hints, and use `E2E_KEEP_REPOS=1` if you need to inspect a failed run's temp
repo.

| Write tests | [`.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/write-tests.md`](.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/write-tests.md) | Scaffold the binary, wire protocol + lifecycle coverage |
| Implement | [`.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/implement.md`](.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/implement.md) | Build the binary using protocol compliance first, lifecycle second, unit tests last |

The skill auto-discovers per AI tool:

| Codex | `AGENTS.md` | "Build an external agent" |

| OpenCode | `.opencode/plugins/` | "Build an external agent" |

`test` tasks. The shared runner falls back to Go defaults when only `go.mod`

### Before You Submit

- **Related issue exists and is approved** -- Your PR references an issue

  corrections, wording-only updates, and maintainer-scoped starter tasks.)
- **Formatting passes** -- `mise run fmt` leaves the tree clean.
- **Linting passes** -- `golangci-lint` clean.
- **Tests pass** -- `mise run test` for unit tests; `mise run test:e2e` if

- **Entire checkpoint trailers included** -- See

3. **Describe your changes** -- Link the related issue, name which agent(s)

# First-Time Contributors

Welcome. This guide is for people who are new to Entire, new to open source,
or just want a careful path through their first contribution to this
repository -- the home of standalone external agent binaries
(`entire-agent-<name>`) that extend the
[Entire CLI](https://github.com/entireio/cli).

The main contribution rules live in [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md).
Treat that file as the source of truth. This page slows the process down and
explains where to start, what to say, what to run, and what to expect after
you open a pull request.

## Who This Is For

Start here if any of these are true:

- You have never opened a pull request before.
- You have contributed to other projects, but not to Entire.
- You want help finding a contribution that is small enough to finish.
- You are unsure how to ask maintainers for the right amount of context.

If you are already comfortable with this repo, use the shorter workflow in
[CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Choose a First Contribution

Start by browsing
[GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/external-agents/issues) for issues
that describe behavior you can reproduce, mention a command or workflow you
can try locally, or feel concrete enough that you can explain the problem
back in your own words. You can also check the `#looking-for-contributors`
channel in [Discord](https://discord.gg/jZJs3Tue4S). You do not need to
understand the whole project before asking about an issue.

Good first contributions are small, clear, and easy to review. For this repo,
that usually means one of these:

- Reproducing a bug in an existing agent (`entire-agent-kiro` or
  `entire-agent-pi`) and adding the missing test.
- Clarifying a confusing message in an agent's CLI output.
- Adding a focused test around existing protocol or lifecycle behavior.
- Tightening a lifecycle assertion in `e2e/` that is currently lax.
- Improving README, agent README, or contributor instructions after you hit
  real friction.

When looking at an issue, favor ones where you can explain the problem back
in your own words. It is okay if you do not know the fix yet. If an issue is
broad, comment with the part you think you can tackle and ask whether that
slice would be useful.

If you do not already have a specific problem in mind, ask in
`#looking-for-contributors` and mention what you are comfortable with, such
as Go tests, CLI output, protocol JSON, lifecycle assertions, or README
wording. A maintainer can usually point you toward a safer slice than
browsing alone can.

**Not a first-PR shape:** adding a brand-new `entire-agent-<name>`. That work
is long-running, involves protocol design choices, and almost always spans
multiple pull requests. If that is what you ultimately want to do, get
comfortable with the repo on something smaller first, then open an issue to
scope the new agent.

Also avoid, for a first PR: changes to the lifecycle harness's `TestMain` /
agent discovery, changes to the protocol-compliance workflow, and anything
that changes how checkpoints or hooks are installed -- unless a maintainer
has already helped define the scope.

## Comment Before You Start

Before starting non-trivial code work, leave a short comment on the issue or
start a new issue. This helps avoid duplicated effort and gives maintainers
a chance to redirect you before you spend time on the wrong approach.

A good first comment is specific:

```text
Hi, I am new to Entire external agents and would like to work on this.

I was able to reproduce the issue by running:

  E2E_AGENT=kiro mise run test:e2e

My plan is to <describe the change> in
agents/entire-agent-kiro/<file or area> and add a focused test for the
behavior. Does that sound like the right direction?
```

If you are not starting from an existing issue, open one with the smallest
concrete problem you can describe:

```text
I hit confusing behavior while running `entire-agent-kiro <subcommand>` on
macOS.

Expected: <what you thought would happen>
Actual: <what actually happened, with the JSON output if relevant>

I can reproduce this locally. Would a small PR that fixes the message and
adds a focused unit test be useful?
```

You do not need a perfect plan. Showing what you have tried and where you are
headed is usually enough.

## Set Up the Repository

Fork the repository on GitHub, then clone your fork:

```bash
git clone git@github.com:YOUR-USERNAME/external-agents.git
cd external-agents
```

Add the upstream repository so you can pull in maintainer changes later:

```bash
git remote add upstream git@github.com:entireio/external-agents.git
git fetch upstream
```

Install the local toolchain:

```bash
mise trust
mise install
mise run build
```

`mise run build` builds every agent binary into `./bin`. Verify the setup
with the unit test suite:

```bash
mise run test
```

If you plan to touch the lifecycle harness, also install the relevant agent's
own CLI (`kiro`, `pi`, ...) so the harness can drive it. Each agent's README
under [`agents/`](../agents/) lists its requirements.

If setup fails, include the command you ran, the full error text, your OS,
and the output of `go version` and `mise --version` when asking for help.

## Create a Branch

Create a branch from the latest `main`:

```bash
git switch main
git pull upstream main
git switch -c fix/short-description
```

Use a branch name that describes the change. Examples:

- `fix/kiro-clearer-missing-config-error`
- `test/pi-transcript-token-edge-case`
- `docs/lifecycle-setup-troubleshooting`

## Make a Small Change

Keep your first pull request narrow. A focused PR is easier to review and
easier to finish.

Good first PR shapes for this repo:

- One failing behavior in a single agent, plus its test.
- One small CLI message improvement in `entire-agent-kiro` or
  `entire-agent-pi`.
- One test-only clarification or assertion tightening.
- One README or setup clarification based on a real problem you hit.

Avoid bundling unrelated cleanup with your first PR. If you notice extra
things while working, leave yourself a note and open a follow-up issue or PR
later.

If you find yourself touching more than one agent, or both the agent and the
shared lifecycle harness, pause and ask whether the change should be split.

## Use AI Carefully

This repository is, in part, about coding-agent integration -- so it is
completely normal to use a coding agent while contributing here. There is no
need to tell us that you used AI.

Use whatever agent and workflow you like. The important rule is that you are
responsible for the final code, tests, and docs. Before submitting a PR,
review the diff yourself. PRs that look generated, unreviewed, or "vibe
coded" without a human pass may be closed.

Quick responsible-AI tips:

- **Think first.** Agents tend to jump straight to code. Ask the agent to
  explore the codebase first, explain the relevant architecture (especially
  the [external agent protocol spec](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/docs/architecture/external-agent-protocol.md)),
  and propose an approach before it edits files.
- **Push back on shortcuts.** Watch for trivial tests, overly wide types,
  optional fields added just to satisfy the compiler, swallowed errors, and
  patterns copied from one agent into another that do not actually fit.
- **Notice uncertainty.** If the agent keeps declaring it understands the
  issue but the patches are not converging, stop and reframe. Use what you
  learned to start a smaller attempt.
- **Cut the bloat.** Remove redundant comments, just-in-case logging,
  over-defensive branches, and tests that only check implementation details
  instead of user-visible or protocol-visible behavior.

## Run the Right Checks

For wording-only changes, run a lightweight sanity check:

```bash
git diff --check
```

For Go code changes in a single agent, run:

```bash
mise run fmt
mise run test
```

For changes that touch the shared lifecycle harness or protocol surface, also
run:

```bash
mise run test:e2e
```

You can narrow lifecycle runs while iterating:

```bash
E2E_AGENT=kiro mise run test:e2e
```

Protocol compliance runs in CI against every built binary -- you do not
normally need to run it locally. If you want to mirror it, build first
(`mise run build`) and then run `external-agents-tests --binary-path
./bin/entire-agent-<name>` against the binary you care about.

Do not assume tests passing locally is enough on its own. The GitHub Actions
workflow runs the protocol compliance suite against every agent on every PR
-- watch the PR checks after you push.

## Commit Your Work

Commit with a short, descriptive message. When your change touches a single
agent, prefix the subject with the agent name:

```bash
git add <files you changed>
git commit -m "kiro: clarify error when config is missing"
```

Cross-cutting changes (the lifecycle harness, shared docs, CI) can omit the
prefix.

Entire is used to dogfood Entire. If you have the Entire CLI installed and
enabled in this repository, the git hook may add an `Entire-Checkpoint`
trailer to your commit message automatically. That is expected. See
[Using Entire While Contributing](../CONTRIBUTING.md#using-entire-while-contributing)
for the full details.

## Open a Pull Request

Push your branch to your fork:

```bash
git push -u origin fix/short-description
```

Then open a pull request against `entireio/external-agents` on GitHub.

In the PR description, include:

- The issue it addresses, if there is one.
- Which agent(s) are affected (e.g. `entire-agent-kiro`) or "shared
  lifecycle harness".
- A short summary of what changed.
- The checks you ran, such as `mise run test`, `mise run test:e2e`, or
  `git diff --check`.
- Anything you want reviewers to pay special attention to.

If your PR is not ready for final review yet, open it as a draft. Draft PRs
are useful when you want early feedback on direction.

## Respond to Review

Review is part of the contribution, not a sign that you did something wrong.
PRs here may receive automated Copilot comments and maintainer comments.

For each review comment:

- If it is right, push a follow-up commit that addresses it.
- If you are unsure, ask a question on the PR.
- If you disagree, explain your reasoning briefly and respectfully.

After pushing updates, leave a short comment saying what changed. GitHub does
not always make it obvious which comments were addressed by a new commit.

## If You Get Stuck

Ask early, and include context. Good help requests include:

- What you are trying to do.
- The command you ran (and `E2E_AGENT=...` if relevant).
- The exact error or output -- the raw JSON line if a protocol check failed.
- What you already checked.
- Your OS, Go version, and `mise --version` when setup or tests are
  involved.

Useful places to ask:

- The GitHub issue you are working on.
- The pull request, if one is already open.
- [Discord](https://discord.gg/jZJs3Tue4S) for general questions.

## Quick Checklist

Before opening your first PR:

- You picked a small, focused change in a single area.
- You asked for maintainer scope before non-trivial code work.
- You created a branch from current `main`.
- You ran the checks that match your change (`mise run test`, and
  `mise run test:e2e` if lifecycle-relevant).
- Your PR description names the affected agent(s) and explains what changed
  and how you tested it.

Thank you for taking the time to contribute. Small, careful improvements
make the project easier for the next person too.
